_comment: Managed R2 object-lifecycle rules for the tc-atlas-rt bucket. Source of truth for apply_lifecycle.py, which merges these BY ID into any rules already on the bucket (it never blind-overwrites unmanaged rules). Prefixes are version-pinned (rt-vN) exactly like the GCS ir_cache_lifecycle.json rules — bump them when _GCS_RT_VERSION bumps.

rules._comment: Per-frame immutable raw-Tb objects (RAW_PERFRAME path) + superseded position-variants. Frames roll off the 6 h window and best-track position revisions orphan old keys; 2 days is well past any reference. The tiny manifest.json is rewritten each cycle and also expires + is recreated, which is harmless.

Global IR mosaic tiles (build_ir_mosaic.py --r2). Each 10-min timestamp's tiles are immutable; the manifest keeps only the last ~18 (R2_KEEP_FRAMES, ~3 h), so older per-timestamp tile sets orphan quickly. 1 day is well past the hot window. frames.json lives at mosaic-v1/ir/frames.json and is rewritten every cycle, so the prefix-match expiry on it is harmless. Bump the mosaic-v1 prefix to invalidate.

v2 RGB mosaic is RETIRED (v3 idx sole builder since 2026-06-27; deploy_mosaic_job.sh guarded behind FORCE_V2=1). This drains the leftover tiles, including the orphans from the accidental 2026-07-23 re-enable. If v2 is ever force-redeployed as a rollback it rewrites fresh tiles each cycle, so a 1-day expiry never bites.

v3 idx mosaic (ir/wv/vis) — the LIVE builder. The job itself prunes its 54-hour rolling archive, so this is only a backstop for orphans (position-revision keys, frames dropped from the manifest, failed prunes). 4 days > the 54 h archive window with margin — must never undercut it or live compare-panel tiles would vanish. frames.json/pack indexes are rewritten every cycle; expiry keys off upload time, so they never expire in practice.
